newsitem.title: UK: UK LABOUR PLEDGES ANNUAL PERFORMANCE AUDIT.
newsitem.headline: UK LABOUR PLEDGES ANNUAL PERFORMANCE AUDIT.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government said on Friday it planned to produce an annual audit reviewing its performance compared with the targets it has set.

Speaking as the government marked 100 days in office since its landslide May 1 election victory, Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott said the plan could enable Labour to win a second five-year term if it kept its promises.
"It is our intention to be judged each year to show how far we've gone towards achieving our promises," Prescott said on BBC radio.
"We've said government could be different. In the first 100 days we've captured the mood of change people wanted in this country."
Prescott was due to hold a news conference later on Friday (0930 GMT), outlining the government's achievements in its first 100 days and defending its record.
Minister without portfolio Peter Mandelson said Labour would set itself tough targets.
"Our job is to continue to be accountable to the people of this country," he said on BBC television.
